title: 020 · Why? #8: a matrix moves the grid, the square's area ×5 = det; det 0 goes flat (predict-first, white)

captions.instagram:
NDA Maths · Determinants. The matrix [[2, 1], [1, 3]] reshapes the grid. The square's area becomes…? A 6 · B 5 · C 7 👇

B. A 2×2 matrix moves the whole plane: î lands on its first column (2, 1), ĵ on its second (1, 3).
The unit square becomes a parallelogram of area 2·3 − 1·1 = 5. That's the determinant: how much every area scales.
Traps: 6 uses the diagonal only (forgets the lean); 7 adds the entries.
det = 0? The plane is squashed onto a line: no area left, and no inverse to undo it.

NDA used it in 2026 (II), Q69: unit vectors a, b at 30°, sides a + 3b and 3a + b. Area = |1·1 − 3·3| × ½ = 4.
